2,138-ish hours was my time in Team Fortress 2 in 2019. Since then, it has gone up around 60 hours, and the stunted time is all down to the Bot issues and my repeated attempts to play it. The Bot problems of TF2 are a perfect encapsulation of why VAC doesn't work; it relies too little on automation, too much on manual waves, and there's no work being done in the background to satiate any player who just wants to play Casual.

"But just play community servers". That's [b]NOT[/b] a solution to the problem, that is running away from the issue at hand and circumventing it. Praying to [b][Insert Local Deity of your Religion Here][/b] would be just as effective a solution than just playing on community servers.

Here is the bitter Pill people don't want to swallow, the scroll of truth they continually throw away because what the sought after was too real for them: Valve likes Illegal Gambling. It likes loot boxes, it likes its storefront filled with shoddy asset-flipped games they can't be bothered to sift through or have any semblance of QA for. That is the reality, and people need to start accepting that.

Since 2015, Valve made it big with Lootboxes and weapon skins in CSGO, and since then, has had one thing on their mind, and that has been "How can we players part with their money while still looking like the good guys of PC Gaming?". Turns out, when you have rabid fans who will go for bat to defend you whenever you screw up, you can get away with a lot of stuff. Quelle Surprise that breeds complacency among users and a situation where you can't escape Steam.

The bots of TF2 are emblematic of Valve's Sloth-like tendencies. Unwilling to make any move to solve or fix a problem until they think it's perfection incarnate, lest they be seen as the bad guy or the solution is seen as unfit. VAC itself is antiquated, old hat, a leaky steam pipe system with so many cracks and buckets catching water that it's impossible to ignore. There's a reason players call VAC the derogatory nickname "Valve Allows Cheaters" because...well...they kinda do.

TF2 is infested with Bots because Valve doesn't have the cajones to try anything, because stopping the bots, stemming the flow, does not compute with their focus on making money off of skins, cosmetics, cards, taunts, or really anything else sold via TF2 or the marketplace. Stop playing TF2, Stop using Steam or the very least try to limit your Steam usage (yes, I'm aware of the irony presented here) and play something else on some other platform. Hell, some games are DRM-Free and can be played away from Steam if you download them first.

 If Valve has any sense, they'll listen to the feedback and the reviewbombing and the petition and the calls to action and make TF2 playable again by purging the bots, either with a more effective Anti-Cheat, or with some more technical wizardry. Take note of the usage of the past tense in this sentence. I cannot in good conscience recommend Team Fortress 2 to anyone in the state that it has been in anymore.

The game has been in a basically unplayable state for at least half a decade now due do Valve's negligence in letting bots run free. Botting accounts have never been a good thing but the surge in automated aimbots in particular flooding and shutting down Casual lobbies is the worst thing to plague Team Fortress 2 since the Meet Your Match update.

Sure, maybe us expecting them to fix their 17 year old game might be asking much, but is it really that unreasonable considering Valve are still profiting off Mann.Co store sales even while aimbots have been ruining official Valve servers for years? What the fuck even is a VAC? That's not an anti-cheat system, it's merely a suggestion that cheaters never took to begin with!

The company is downright complicit in the decay of this once great game too, considering they are actively profiting off each botted account because they are all too happy to buy something from the game's digital storefront to circumvent the inability to use communication features - a limitation Valve put out as a bandaid fix to "deal" with the bot crisis in the first place. Real F2P players can't even call out for a Medic in the game without making a purchase! The only people you hurt are real players - and maybe the one bothoster who hasn't figured out how to scam people out of Steam giftcards to feed their bot accounts with the funds to buy themselves the privilege of spamming the voice- and textchat.

To prevent myself for getting too long winded, I'll just pitch into the pile of unfavorable reviews. We may not get our funny shooty game back, even with this last stand of a protest but I'll be damned if I don't leave a mark and expose Valve for their shitty practices at least. Valve aren't game devs anymore, they're just shilling games through Steam and sell virtual hats that you they don't even make themselves.

tl;dr: #FixTF2 , at least give us an actually functioning anti-cheat Jesus Christ, Gabe

166582743.review:
Team Fortress 2 represents many firsts for me. It was my first 3D first-person shooter, it was my first non-Flash game, it was my first PvP game, and it was my first Steam game. I remember bragging about getting the Gibus to my friends at school, and even became indebted to a classmate so I could get a Steam card in order to buy hats. I don't think I ever finished paying that debt off.

I don't play this game much anymore - my tastes in gaming have moved on from PvP first-person shooters. However, the culture surrounding Team Fortress 2 is much more than just the people playing the game. The memes, the animations both serious and silly, the YouTube community, the voice actors, and every single kid that put ragdolls into crude poses in Garry's Mod because they were bored. This is what keeps me around.

Game companies everywhere would give their figurative left nuts to have a property that continues to remain pervasive in not just gaming culture, but Internet culture as a whole, even a decade and a half after it's released. And what does Valve do with this unique blessing?

Nothing. Or, at least, close to nothing.

Surely you've heard about the state the game is in. No major updates in years. Cheating bot accounts ruining games. Promises made, but not kept.

It's not like Valve doesn't care at all. They have indeed made some mid-sized updates ever since the original #SaveTF2 campaign, and have even modified the game to take advantage of modern 64-bit hardware. But there still seems to be a collective unwillingness at Valve to sit down, put their heads together, and finally tackle the fundamental problems that have been plaguing the game for close to 33% of its illustrious lifespan.

I know about Valve’s unique organizational structure that discourages people from working on old, unpopular projects. I know about the messy, disorganized state the game is in under the hood. I know about the constant arms race that cheat creators and cheat detectors are in, a race in which silence is often justified.

But it’s still not an excuse to do so little in such a large span of time.

We don’t even want major updates anymore. Those can wait. We just want something, anything, to remove the near-constant threat of bots that ruin games for novice and veteran players alike. Something that isn’t a band-aid solution, like the silencing of F2P accounts was. Something actually concrete. And if you have been working on something, then tell us. Break the silence.

It’s not a matter of resources – Valve has some of the most talented people in the whole industry, and a near–unlimited source of income from Steam. Even if no one at Valve wants to touch the game, or VAC, with a ten foot pole, surely somebody can be paid to do so.

It’s not even just TF2 anymore – recently even Counter-Strike 2 has been seeing an influx of cheating bots that has caused an outcry from their community and their content creators. It is in Valve’s best interest to fix the issues that affect two of their most popular IPs.

At this point, doing nothing would be Valve shooting themselves in the foot. Sure, they could just sit back and let the cash roll in while leaving one, or even two, of their most popular games to the wolves. They could do that. But what would it cost them? Their reputation of one of the greatest game developers of all time. A game that continues to maintain a stable, if smaller than previously thought, player base despite all the problems that plague it. And finally, a dedicated community that wants nothing more than to see their favorite game rise from the ashes of neglect and abuse.

Valve, do something.

#FixTF2

26/08/24 Edit: Things have indeed changed for the better, but this review is remaining negative until it's clear that more permanent measures are going to be put into place. Still, good on you, Valve.

19/09/24 Edit: With recent good news, I feel confident in switching my review to Positive. Give the game a go if you somehow stumble upon this review. There's no better time than now.

They will also spam voice chat with disruptive audio, flood text chat, mimic and kick actual players, and join as a group making it incredibly difficult to kick them if not jumped on by actual players before they gain a majority

The official anti-cheat (VAC) isn't stopping them and ANY player can see this by jumping into a few matches.

In the event you can find a playable match on an official server, it will be commonplace to have to call vote kicks on these BOTS left and right for the duration of the entire match as new ones join.

-
Valve has made band aid fixes over the years to help address this issue including the removal of the ability of Free-to-Play players to communicate in game, not even able to use in game voice commands to call for a healer, but none have fixed the problem for any significant amount of time since this requires support that we're simply not getting.

We've been 5 years from the last major content update that wasn't community created in-game cosmetics (which Valve profits heavily from) and poorly tested community created maps, or some bug fixes every blue moon.

The code for the majority of these bots is publicly available, which is why community anti-cheat programs work on their servers, getting rid of them is perfectly doable, it's only through lack of care and effort that they exist on Valve servers still, after many years.

This is how Valve rewards loyal players and customers for their continued support over the game's 16 years, with cosmetic lootboxes three times a year while their servers that you get queued to by pressing the giant "PLAY NOW" button are unplayable outside of peak hours and with vigilant players (even then it's not uncommon to be kicked by a bot or mistaken for one).

This game has taken up way too much of my time, despite being actively harmed by playing. It's a community that seems innocuous and welcoming, but hides a huge undercurrent of hate I have not experienced in the most hateful of games. When that negativity surfaces, it transforms into something profoundly harmful and destructive to my mental state, leaving me exhausted for days. I'm done pretending that such feelings are normal.

I'm by no means a sensitive person or player. I grew up on the internet as a gay guy, I have no reason to be soft. However, in the TF2 community, hate goes beyond petty words and into uncanny obsession. I'm frequently attacked by:

- Sadistic friend groups. People who queue or join games together to speed run killing off any fun for others. These groups run Natasha + Vaccinator + Sticky spam combos that dominate the entire game, forcing everyone to re queue repeatedly just to find a normal match. The best part? It's MY fault for not being "good enough at the game". Bitch, if 3.7k hours makes me bad at the game, you need to get a job.

- Nazism. I'm told by people who stalk my profile that I should've been tortured and killed just like the Jews. What kind of inexcusable bullshit is this? Why am I frequently the only one calling out such behavior, and why am I berated for doing so? It's enough to drive a person insane: When everyone around me says I'm wrong, I'm inclined to believe I'm in the wrong and need to reevaluate. Why is it wrong to be against killing minorities?

- Malicious actors. People from both teams look at my profile, see I'm a furry, and aim to make my experience unbearable. Every, single, game, I'm told to kill myself for having a hobby I enjoy and everyone agrees (except for other furries, of course). Part of the game is socializing with others, so ignoring it deletes a chunk of the game specifically because of who I choose to be. Additionally, why do you think I continue to be a furry when those around me who aren't furries constantly throw hateful rhetoric my way?

- Racism. The amount of racism I'm forced to bear witness to is disgusting. I'm frequently the only one to butt into conversations and tell people, "Hey, it's fucked up to hate people just for being black", and almost always get kicked for speaking out against it. If I'm not kicked, the game usually devolves into sadistic friend groups getting angry that people disagree and ruin the match. Most people in TF2 don't seem to understand this, but joking about and/or ignoring racism doesn't exempt you from being a racist.

Finally, the most important, and what's forced me to quit the game:
- [b] A community that doesn't care. [/b]
I find myself being the only one speaking out against really inexcusable behavior, calling out the cruelty that everyone else ignores or condones. Instead of support, I'm met with this huge wave of backlash—my efforts to hold people accountable for being insanely hateful only makes me a target. I've never been more alienated for doing and saying what should be the bare minimum: Treating others with respect.

I can already see the comments I'll receive for pointing these things out. By responding with ‘Get good,’ ‘Stop being so sensitive,’ or ‘It's just a game,’ you’re proving exactly why TF2 has been ruined. It’s not about being weak—it’s about calling attention to a toxic culture where concerns are belittled instead of addressed. When people say "This isn’t a serious problem", it shows how normalized toxicity in TF2 has become. Dismissing the mental health and well-being of others because it's ‘just a game on the internet’ ignores how online spaces affect real lives; The toxicity you’re enabling leaves people like myself feeling unsafe, alienated, and emotionally drained. This has been proven over and over again, and your refusal to believe someone behind a screen is legitimately effected by your demeanor after years of proof is telling of your intelligence.

The highs of connection and belonging I felt when I first played were so intoxicating that I've found it hard to pull away. You can tell yourself it’s just a bad moment, that the good that TF2 offers outweighs the bad, that it's just a game, and before you know it you’re part of the problem- conforming to a community full of degenerates.

Do not play this game. Find a game you can enjoy with your friends, one that doesn't leave you wishing, "Man, maybe I'll have a better day tomorrow". Gaming should be a positive experience you enjoy, not one where you dread getting on because it'll either be great or dehumanizing.
